subject: history_social
passage: In movies, cartoons, and costumes, Viking warriors are almost always shown wearing helmets with large horns. This image has become so familiar that many people assume it reflects how the Vikings really dressed for battle.
passage_b: Archaeologists have found no evidence that Vikings wore horned helmets. The only nearly complete Viking helmet ever discovered, found in Norway, is a simple rounded iron cap with no horns. Historians trace the popular image largely to the 1800s, when costume designers for operas and plays added horns to make Viking characters look dramatic.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the assumption in Text 1?

choices.A: By agreeing that Vikings often wore horned helmets in battle
choices.B: By arguing that the familiar image is not supported by evidence
choices.C: By claiming that Vikings never wore helmets of any kind at all
choices.D: By suggesting that horned helmets were common in 1800s Norway

explanation.why: Text 1 says many people assume the horned helmet "reflects how the Vikings really dressed." Text 2 says archaeologists "have found no evidence" of horned helmets and traces the image to costume designers of the 1800s. So the author of Text 2 would say the assumption lacks support.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says there is "no evidence" that Vikings wore horned helmets.
explanation.B: Correct. Text 2 explains that no horned Viking helmets have been found and that the image came from 1800s stage costumes.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 describes a real Viking helmet, a "rounded iron cap," so it does not say Vikings wore no helmets.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 says costume designers in the 1800s added horns for the stage, not that horned helmets were common in Norway then.
